scenes.text: Imagine walking into your bedroom and slowly being poisoned by your own walls.
In the Victorian era, a vibrant new shade called Scheele's Green became an absolute sensation, used in dresses, toys, and wallpapers.
This gorgeous green got its brilliance from copper arsenite, and when damp Victorian homes grew humid, a toxic fungus released deadly gas into the bedrooms.
Entire families fell mysteriously ill before doctors realized the killer was literally the wallpaper, so would you have noticed the warning signs?
